subject: MSA + Order Form: DPA redlines, SCCs, and subprocessor evidence (ClearPath)
message_1_body:
Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — we’re moving fast on the procurement side. Attached are our redlines for the MSA and the Data Processing Addendum; we also included the SCCs annex our legal team prefers. The procurement team (cc’d) has a target to finalize by 11/12.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm Redwood can provide a current subprocessor list and SOC2 evidence?
- We’ve proposed: 30 days’ notice for subprocessor additions, and a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) carve-out for specific EU-hosted data flows — please confirm feasibility.
- There’s a new clause in our DPA (Section 4.3) requesting a secondary-data-handback on termination — we need to know if that is acceptable or if Redwood can offer an alternative mitigation.

I’ve attached: ClearPath_MSA_DPA_redline_20261028.pdf and ClearPath_SCCs_Annex.pdf for your legal team to review. Would you share an expected timeline for legal comments and any required evidence?

Regards,
Elena Martinez
Head of Procurement
ClearPath Health

message_3_subject: RE: Redlines: initial legal read (MSA + DPA)
message_3_body:
Vanessa — initial notes from legal after a first pass. I attached a tracked-changes file with inline comments (Redwood_DPA_KI_comments_20261029.docx). Key items to consider: 

1) Section: Liability / Cap in Order Form — ClearPath has proposed a carveout that effectively removes the cap for certain data incidents. We should push back to maintain our standard cap but can consider a modest increase tied to order value.

2) Section: Subprocessors — proposed 30 days’ notice is acceptable; however we require the ability to use subcontractors for managed infra. Suggest redline: ‘30 days’ notice for material changes; emergency additions allowed with after-the-fact notice.’

3) Section: Data handback on termination — the ‘secondary-data-handback’ asks for a physical transfer and escrow-like custody; that is high-touch and operationally risky. Alternative: offer certified secure export in standard formats and a three-month data retrieval window with logging of exports (we can add a TIA reference to document the flows).

4) SCCs annex — OK in principle, but we need to add a schedule mapping our subprocessors to SCC Annexes and an acceptance process for any delegation of BCR/SCC responsibilities. Ask privacy to validate.

Next steps (proposal):
- Monica to request SOC2 report + subprocessor CSV from ClearPath (ask for org-wide vs. per-env).
- Legal to produce a redline counter by 11/04, highlighting the liability/handback alternative and a subprocessor notice clause.
- Sales to confirm if EU-only hosting is required and provide pricing delta.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_KI_comments_20261029.docx (tracked changes)
message_4_subject: Re: Redlines: DPA evidence and TIA scope
message_4_body:
Vanessa / team — I’ll take the evidence request. Elena — can you confirm the following as separate artifacts: 

- Current SOC2 Type II report (last 12 months),
- Subprocessor list with roles and subprocessor geographies (CSV preferred),
- Any existing TIAs you have for third-party transfers (we want to understand their baseline),
- Specific data categories that ClearPath considers EU-restricted (PHI / special categories).

Note on cost: if ClearPath requires strict EU-only hosting for all customer data and prohibits routing through non-EU subprocessors, we will need to model an EU-only deployment (dedicated capacity/region). Rough ballpark: ~20% uplift on committed capacity and an expected one-time onboarding fee for data residency controls. Ben — can you put rough numbers against that for the deal?

Monica Patel
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
message_5_subject: Re: Pricing impact for EU-only hosting (ballpark)
message_5_body:
Quick numbers: if ClearPath requires an EU-only deployment for production traffic and no cross-border subprocessors, estimate: 
- Committed monthly capacity uplift: +20% (~$6,000/mo on a $30k/mo commit)
- One-time onboarding/migration: $18,000 (includes secure data export and verification)
- Optional SLA premium: +10% on committed rate

These are preliminary — can refine after we understand the scope in the subprocessor CSV. For HubSpot: deal CPH-2026-0817; I’ll tag these values in the quote.

— Ben
message_6_subject: Re: Redlines: DPA evidence and subprocessor list attached
message_6_body:
Vanessa / Karthik / Monica — thanks for the quick turn. Attached are: subprocessor_list_clearpath_20261102.csv (lists our vendors and geo), and ClearPath_SOC2_Attestation_20261102.pdf.

A few clarifications from our side:
- We can provide the subprocessor list and SOC2 attestation (attached).
- We prefer the SCCs annex approach and can accept a 30-day notice for non-material subprocessor changes. For emergency additions, we ask for notice ‘as soon as possible’ with an after-the-fact confirmation.
- On the handback clause: we cannot commit to a physical escrow/handback process as written. We propose the alternative language: ‘Customer may request secure export of Customer Data in encrypted standard formats within 90 days of termination; Provider will cooperate with documented export procedures and will maintain logs of export events.’ We hope this aligns with Redwood’s alternative.

Timeline: procurement is aiming to execute before 11/12. Can Redwood provide the counter-redline and evidence confirmation by 11/04?

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Procurement
ClearPath Health
